explanation_en: 'A contrarreloj' (or 'contra reloj') means to work or race against the clock, under intense time pressure. It is a fixed adverbial locution used frequently in news reports, sports, and professional environments to emphasize that time is running out.

examples.en_text: We had to work against the clock to submit the project before midnight.
examples.target_text: Tuvimos que trabajar a contrarreloj para entregar el proyecto antes de la medianoche.

examples.en_text: The student reviewed the notes against the clock right before entering the exam.
examples.target_text: El estudiante repasó los apuntes a contrarreloj justo antes de entrar al examen.

examples.en_text: We missed the bus and had to run against the clock so we wouldn't miss our flight.
examples.target_text: Perdimos el autobús y tuvimos que correr a contrarreloj para no perder el vuelo.

examples.en_text: The concert organizers are preparing the stage against the clock.
examples.target_text: Los organizadores del concierto están preparando el escenario a contrarreloj.

examples.en_text: The chef cooked against the clock because the customers were already waiting at the table.
examples.target_text: El chef cocinó a contrarreloj porque los clientes ya estaban esperando en la mesa.

examples.en_text: The firefighters worked against the clock to put out the fire before it reached the forest.
examples.target_text: Los bomberos trabajaron a contrarreloj para apagar el incendio antes de que llegara al bosque.

idiom: nada más y nada menos que
explanation_en: 'Nada más y nada menos que' is an emphatic idiomatic formula used to highlight a surprising, significant, or impressive fact, equivalent to 'none other than' or 'nothing less than'. It is highly common in both spoken Spanish and journalism to draw attention to a specific detail or participant.

examples.en_text: Tonight's guest of honor is none other than the director of the movie.
examples.target_text: El invitado de honor de esta noche es nada más y nada menos que el director de la película.

examples.en_text: For her birthday, she received nothing less than a trip to Paris.
examples.target_text: Para su cumpleaños, recibió nada más y nada menos que un viaje a París.

examples.en_text: The new museum cost nothing less than ten million euros.
examples.target_text: El nuevo museo ha costado nada más y nada menos que diez millones de euros.

examples.en_text: Yesterday I ran into none other than my first school teacher on the street.
examples.target_text: Ayer me encontré en la calle con nada más y nada menos que mi primer profesor de escuela.

examples.en_text: They offered him a position in none other than the company's headquarters.
examples.target_text: Le ofrecieron un puesto en nada más y nada menos que la sede central de la empresa.

examples.en_text: To pass this exam, you have to study nothing less than three hundred pages.
examples.target_text: Para aprobar este examen, tienes que estudiar nada más y nada menos que trescientas páginas.

explanation_en: 'Pisar callos' (literally 'to step on bunions/corns') is the Spanish equivalent of 'to step on someone's toes' or 'to ruffle feathers'. It is used when someone's actions or words offend or challenge powerful people or sensitive interests, and is common in political and workplace contexts.

examples.en_text: In this office, it's better to be careful not to step on anyone's toes.
examples.target_text: En esta oficina es mejor tener cuidado para no pisar callos.

examples.en_text: I think I stepped on some toes yesterday when I criticized the new project.
examples.target_text: Creo que pisé algunos callos ayer cuando critiqué el nuevo proyecto.

examples.en_text: If you want to propose changes, do it tactfully so you don't step on any toes.
examples.target_text: Si quieres proponer cambios, hazlo con tacto para que no pises callos.

examples.en_text: The new director is stepping on a lot of toes with his reorganization plan.
examples.target_text: El nuevo director está pisando muchos callos con su plan de reorganización.

examples.en_text: Sometimes it's impossible to tell the truth without stepping on toes.
examples.target_text: A veces es imposible decir la verdad sin pisar callos.

examples.en_text: If you decide to change the rules now, you are going to step on more than one person's toes.
examples.target_text: Si decides cambiar las reglas ahora, vas a pisar más de un callo.

explanation_en: 'A puerta cerrada' means 'behind closed doors' or 'in private'. It is a standard legal and journalistic collocation used to describe meetings, trials, or sports matches that take place without the public or press being present.

examples.en_text: The board of directors met behind closed doors to discuss the future of the company.
examples.target_text: La junta directiva se reunió a puerta cerrada para discutir el futuro de la empresa.

examples.en_text: Due to the penalty, the next soccer match will be played behind closed doors.
examples.target_text: Debido a la sanción, el próximo partido de fútbol se jugará a puerta cerrada.

examples.en_text: The two presidents spoke behind closed doors for more than three hours.
examples.target_text: Los dos presidentes hablaron a puerta cerrada durante más de tres horas.

examples.en_text: The trial was held behind closed doors to protect the identity of the witnesses.
examples.target_text: El juicio se celebró a puerta cerrada para proteger la identidad de los testigos.

examples.en_text: My parents always solve their problems behind closed doors, never in front of us.
examples.target_text: Mis padres siempre solucionan sus problemas a puerta cerrada, nunca delante de nosotros.

examples.en_text: The school principal spoke with the student behind closed doors about his behavior.
examples.target_text: El director del colegio habló con el estudiante a puerta cerrada sobre su comportamiento.

explanation_en: 'El visto bueno' (often abbreviated as 'Vº Bº') means 'the green light', 'approval', or 'endorsement'. It is a highly common administrative and everyday expression used when an authority, boss, or official approves a document, plan, or agreement.

examples.en_text: The boss already gave the green light to the project, so we can start tomorrow.
examples.target_text: El jefe ya dio el visto bueno al proyecto, así que podemos empezar mañana.

examples.en_text: We are waiting for the finance department's approval to buy the equipment.
examples.target_text: Estamos esperando el visto bueno del departamento de finanzas para comprar los equipos.

examples.en_text: My parents gave my new boyfriend their approval as soon as they met him.
examples.target_text: Mis padres le dieron el visto bueno a mi nuevo novio en cuanto lo conocieron.

examples.en_text: Before sending the contract to the client, I need the lawyer's approval.
examples.target_text: Antes de enviar el contrato al cliente, necesito el visto bueno del abogado.

examples.en_text: The festival finally received the city council's green light to be held in the park.
examples.target_text: El festival finalmente recibió el visto bueno del ayuntamiento para celebrarse en el parque.

examples.en_text: Can you look at this design and give me your approval before I publish it?
examples.target_text: ¿Puedes mirar este diseño y darme tu visto bueno antes de que lo publique?

explanation_en: The expression 'dar un respiro' literally translates to 'to give a breath.' Idiomatically, it means to provide a temporary break, respite, or relief from a stressful or difficult situation. It is commonly used in news reports and daily conversation when discussing weather, work pressure, or ongoing crises.

examples.en_text: Finally finishing this report gives me a breather before the next meeting.
examples.target_text: Terminar este informe por fin me da un respiro antes de la próxima reunión.

examples.en_text: The rain stopped in the afternoon and gave us a breather so we could go out for a walk.
examples.target_text: La lluvia paró por la tarde y nos dio un respiro para poder salir a caminar.

examples.en_text: The boss decided to give us a breather and changed the deadline to Monday.
examples.target_text: El jefe decidió darnos un respiro y cambió la fecha de entrega para el lunes.

examples.en_text: Getting this new job will give me some breathing room with the rent payment.
examples.target_text: Conseguir este nuevo trabajo me dará un respiro con el pago del alquiler.

examples.en_text: My phone is not giving me a break today; it won't stop ringing with messages from clients.
examples.target_text: Mi teléfono no me da un respiro hoy; no para de sonar con mensajes de clientes.

examples.en_text: This medicine is very good because it gives my body a break when I have allergies.
examples.target_text: Esta medicina es muy buena porque le da un respiro a mi cuerpo cuando tengo alergia.

explanation_en: 'A toda prisa' is a very common adverbial locution meaning 'at full speed' or 'in a great hurry.' It is more idiomatic and expressive than simply using 'muy rápido' or 'rápidamente.' It is typically paired with motion verbs like 'salir,' 'correr,' or 'ir.'

examples.en_text: I had to leave the office in a great hurry because I forgot I had a doctor's appointment.
examples.target_text: Tuve que salir de la oficina a toda prisa porque olvidé que tenía una cita médica.

examples.en_text: The taxi was going at full speed down the avenue to get to the airport on time.
examples.target_text: El taxi iba a toda prisa por la avenida para llegar al aeropuerto a tiempo.

examples.en_text: We had to clean the house in a great hurry before the guests arrived.
examples.target_text: Tuvimos que limpiar la casa a toda prisa antes de que llegaran los invitados.

examples.en_text: Since the exam was ending in five minutes, I answered the last questions in a great hurry.
examples.target_text: Como el examen terminaba en cinco minutos, respondí las últimas preguntas a toda prisa.

examples.en_text: The firefighters arrived at full speed to put out the fire in the building.
examples.target_text: Los bomberos llegaron a toda prisa para apagar el fuego en el edificio.

examples.en_text: We had to finish the report in a great hurry because the boss wanted it for today.
examples.target_text: Tuvimos que terminar el informe a toda prisa porque el jefe lo quería para hoy.

idiom: con los ojos siempre puestos en
explanation_en: The figurative expression 'tener/poner los ojos puestos en algo' means to watch something vigilantly, to focus one's attention on it, or to keep a close eye on it. It is highly natural and used to describe intense focus, monitoring, or aspiration. Note that the preposition 'en' is essential to connect to the object of focus.

examples.en_text: She works hard every day, with her eyes always on her children's future.
examples.target_text: Ella trabaja duro todos los días, con los ojos siempre puestos en el futuro de sus hijos.

examples.en_text: The forward ran toward the goal with his eyes always on the ball.
examples.target_text: El delantero corrió hacia la portería con los ojos siempre puestos en el balón.

examples.en_text: The company keeps growing, with its eyes always on the international market.
examples.target_text: La empresa sigue creciendo, con los ojos siempre puestos en el mercado internacional.

examples.en_text: He took the exam with his eyes always on the clock so he wouldn't run out of time.
examples.target_text: Hizo el examen con los ojos siempre puestos en el reloj para no quedarse sin tiempo.

examples.en_text: She studied for months with her eyes always on getting the scholarship.
examples.target_text: Estudió durante meses con los ojos siempre puestos en conseguir la beca.

examples.en_text: We walked along the trail with our eyes always on the map so we wouldn't get lost.
examples.target_text: Caminábamos por el sendero con los ojos siempre puestos en el mapa para no perdernos.

explanation_en: 'De inmediato' is a set adverbial phrase meaning 'immediately' or 'right away.' While 'inmediatamente' is also common, 'de inmediato' sounds slightly more formal and is highly favored in journalism, literature, and professional contexts. It is constructed with the preposition 'de' followed by the adjective 'inmediato' acting as a noun.

examples.en_text: If you have any questions, please write to me and I will answer you right away.
examples.target_text: Si tienes alguna pregunta, por favor escríbeme y te responderé de inmediato.

examples.en_text: The patient needs to see a doctor immediately; we cannot wait any longer.
examples.target_text: El paciente necesita ver a un médico de inmediato; no podemos esperar más.

examples.en_text: When I turned off the computer, the screen went black immediately.
examples.target_text: Cuando apagué el ordenador, la pantalla se puso negra de inmediato.

examples.en_text: Upon arriving at the hotel, they gave us the room keys right away.
examples.target_text: Al llegar al hotel, nos dieron las llaves de la habitación de inmediato.

examples.en_text: You have to clean up this mess immediately before your parents arrive.
examples.target_text: Tienes que limpiar este desastre de inmediato antes de que lleguen tus padres.

examples.en_text: The director read the proposal and knew immediately that it would be a great success.
examples.target_text: El director leyó la propuesta y supo de inmediato que sería un gran éxito.

explanation_en: 'Hacer cuentas' literally means 'to do accounts' or 'to calculate.' Idiomatically, it means to assess a situation financially, to calculate costs, damages, or to reflect on the consequences of an event. It is a very common colloquial and journalistic expression used when evaluating the aftermath of a disaster or planning a budget.

examples.en_text: We have to do the math before deciding whether to buy the new car.
examples.target_text: Tenemos que hacer cuentas antes de decidir si compramos el coche nuevo.

examples.en_text: Yesterday I did the math and realized that we spent too much on advertising this month.
examples.target_text: Ayer hice cuentas y me di cuenta de que este mes gastamos demasiado en publicidad.

examples.en_text: Do the math yourself; you'll see that it's cheaper to travel by train than by plane.
examples.target_text: Haz cuentas tú mismo; verás que es más barato viajar en tren que en avión.

examples.en_text: If we do the math, we will see that we can save quite a lot of money by switching suppliers.
examples.target_text: Si hacemos cuentas, veremos que podemos ahorrar bastante dinero cambiando de proveedor.

examples.en_text: I don't think it's a good idea to open the shop without first calculating the monthly expenses.
examples.target_text: No creo que sea una buena idea abrir la tienda sin antes hacer cuentas de los gastos mensuales.

examples.en_text: They did the math and decided that it wasn't worth renting such an expensive commercial space.
examples.target_text: Ellos hicieron cuentas y decidieron que no valía la pena alquilar ese local tan caro.

explanation_en: The construction 'dar [algo] por perdido' means 'to write something off' or 'to consider something lost/hopeless.' The structure 'dar + noun + por + adjective' is a classic Spanish pattern (e.g., 'dar por hecho', 'dar por muerto'). It indicates a definitive mental shift where one accepts that something cannot be recovered or saved.

examples.en_text: Since I have to study for the September exams, I'm already writing off the summer.
examples.target_text: Como tengo que estudiar para los exámenes de septiembre, ya doy el verano por perdido.

examples.en_text: With the construction on the beach, the hotels in the area have already written off the summer.
examples.target_text: Con las obras en la playa, los hoteles de la zona ya han dado el verano por perdido.

examples.en_text: If they cancel this flight too, we can write off the summer.
examples.target_text: Si nos cancelan este vuelo también, podemos dar el verano por perdido.

examples.en_text: Poor Juan, he broke his leg and is already writing off the summer.
examples.target_text: Pobre Juan, se ha roto la pierna y ya da el verano por perdido.

examples.en_text: Don't write off the summer just yet, I'm sure we can go on a quick getaway in August.
examples.target_text: No des el verano por perdido todavía, seguro que podemos hacer una escapada en agosto.

examples.en_text: When the crisis started in June, the company wrote off the summer and closed temporarily.
examples.target_text: Cuando empezó la crisis en junio, la empresa dio el verano por perdido y cerró temporalmente.

explanation_en: 'Dentro del mal, el menos' is a common idiomatic variation of the proverb 'del mal, el menos,' which translates to 'the lesser of two evils' or 'making the best of a bad situation.' It is used to express relief that, despite a bad situation, the outcome was not as catastrophic as it could have been. It is highly conversational and shows a pragmatic, resilient attitude.

examples.en_text: We had to cancel the trip, but at least they refunded all our money; it's the lesser of two evils.
examples.target_text: Tuvimos que cancelar el viaje, pero al menos nos devolvieron todo el dinero; dentro del mal, el menos.

examples.en_text: The car was wrecked in the accident, but no one was hurt. All things considered, it's the lesser of two evils.
examples.target_text: El coche quedó destrozado en el accidente, pero nadie resultó herido. Dentro del mal, el menos.

examples.en_text: I was laid off from the company, but they gave me a good severance package. The lesser of two evils, I suppose.
examples.target_text: Me despidieron de la empresa, pero me dieron una buena indemnización. Dentro del mal, el menos, supongo.

examples.en_text: He broke his arm right before the holidays, but luckily it was the left one. It's the lesser of two evils.
examples.target_text: Se rompió el brazo justo antes de las vacaciones, pero por suerte fue el izquierdo. Dentro del mal, el menos.

examples.en_text: It rained during the wedding, but at least the ceremony was indoors. It's the lesser of two evils.
examples.target_text: Llovió durante la boda, pero al menos la ceremonia era bajo techo. Dentro del mal, el menos.

examples.en_text: We lost some clients this month, but we managed to keep the most important ones. It's the lesser of two evils.
examples.target_text: Perdimos algunos clientes este mes, pero logramos mantener a los más importantes. Dentro del mal, el menos.
